questions.stem: Put the stages of a frog's life cycle in the right order.
sequence: a tadpole with a tail and gills
a froglet with a short tail
questions.explanation: A frog starts as an egg, hatches into a tadpole, grows legs, becomes a froglet and finally an adult frog that can live on land.

questions.stem: A seed ___ into a seedling, and a chick ___ from an egg.
questions.explanation: When a seed starts to grow we say it germinates. A chick comes out of its egg when it hatches.

questions.stem: Match each young animal or plant to what it grows into.
questions.explanation: A tadpole grows into a frog, a caterpillar becomes a butterfly, a chick grows into a hen and a seedling grows into an adult plant.

questions.stem: Which features are inherited from parents? Sort them.
questions.explanation: Features such as eye colour and fur colour are passed from parents to young. Scars, haircuts and languages are not inherited: they come from what happens to you or what you learn.

questions.stem: What do we call the small differences between living things of the same kind, such as kittens of different colours?
options: metamorphosis
germination
variation
migration
questions.explanation: Variation means differences between living things of the same kind. Young are like their parents but never exactly the same.

questions.stem: Tanvir says, 'If I build big muscles at the gym, my children will be born with big muscles.' Is he right?
questions.explanation: Features you gain during your life, like big muscles or a scar, are not inherited. Only features carried from your parents, like eye colour, are passed on.

questions.stem: What do plants need to grow well? Choose all that are right.
options: light
water
air
minerals from the soil
meat
plastic
questions.explanation: Plants need light, water, air, warmth and minerals from the soil. They make their own food, so they do not need meat.

questions.stem: Compare the life cycles of a chicken and a frog. Which statements are right? Choose all that are right.
options: Both start life as an egg.
A chick changes its body shape a lot, like a tadpole does.
A tadpole breathes with gills and later grows lungs.
A chick looks like a small adult when it hatches.
A frog's young stage lives on dry land.
questions.explanation: Both hatch from eggs. A tadpole lives in water and changes shape (metamorphosis), but a chick already looks like a small hen.

questions.stem: Why does a butterfly lay its eggs on a leaf and not on a stone?
questions.model_answer: When the caterpillar hatches it needs leaves to eat, so the eggs are laid on a plant where it has food straight away.
questions.explanation: A caterpillar hatches hungry and eats leaves all the time. Laying eggs on the right plant gives the young caterpillars food from the start.

questions.stem: Sort these young animals by how they look compared with the adult.
categories: Looks very different from the adult
items: Looks very different from the adult
Looks very different from the adult
Looks very different from the adult
questions.explanation: A tadpole, a caterpillar and a silkworm change their body shape completely as they grow. This is metamorphosis. Chicks, kittens and calves just grow bigger.

questions.stem: What does a seed need to germinate?
options: light only
water and warmth
soil only
wind
questions.explanation: A seed needs water and the right temperature to start to grow. Light is needed later, once the seedling has leaves.

questions.stem: A big change of body shape as an animal grows up is called ___.
questions.explanation: Frogs and butterflies go through metamorphosis. Their young look very different from the adults.

questions.stem: A chicken goes through metamorphosis, like a butterfly does.
questions.explanation: A chick looks like a small version of the adult hen. Butterflies and frogs change their body shape completely, but chickens do not.

questions.stem: Look at the frog's life cycle. Which stage comes straight after the tadpole?
questions.image_alt: The life cycle of a frog: eggs (frogspawn), tadpole, froglet, adult frog.
options: eggs (frogspawn)
adult frog
froglet
chrysalis
questions.explanation: The tadpole grows legs and loses its tail to become a froglet, and then an adult frog.

questions.stem: Look at the butterfly's life cycle. What happens to the caterpillar inside the chrysalis (pupa)?
questions.image_alt: The life cycle of a butterfly: eggs, caterpillar, chrysalis, adult butterfly.
options: It lays more eggs.
It sleeps and wakes up as a bigger caterpillar.
Its body changes completely into an adult butterfly.
It turns into a tadpole.
questions.explanation: The chrysalis is a resting stage. Inside it, the caterpillar's body changes completely until an adult butterfly comes out.

questions.stem: Look at the chicken's life cycle. Which statement is right?
questions.image_alt: The life cycle of a chicken: egg, hatching, chick, adult hen.
options: A chick has a tail and gills like a tadpole.
A chick looks like a small hen when it hatches.
A chick goes into a chrysalis.
A hen turns back into an egg.
questions.explanation: A chicken's life cycle has no big change of shape. The chick hatches looking like a small adult and just grows bigger.

questions.stem: Which numbered stage shows the seed starting to grow into a seedling (germination)?
questions.image_alt: The life cycle of a flowering plant with seven stages numbered 1 to 7.
questions.explanation: Stage 2 is germination. Stage 1 is the seed, stage 5 is pollination and stage 7 is seed dispersal.

questions.stem: Use the picture of the flowering plant's life cycle. Put the stages in order, starting with the seed.
questions.image_alt: The life cycle of a flowering plant with stages numbered: seed, germination, young plant, flowering, pollination, fertilisation and fruit, seed dispersal.
questions.explanation: A seed germinates into a young plant that flowers. Pollen is carried between flowers (pollination), seeds form in a fruit and the seeds are scattered, ready to grow into new plants.

questions.stem: Match each young stage to the adult it grows into.
questions.explanation: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly, a baby chick grows into a hen and a seedling grows into a plant that makes flowers.

questions.stem: Arif grew cress seedlings in a dark cupboard. They grew tall, but they were pale yellow and thin. What should he do to help them become healthy plants?
options: Give them less water.
Keep them in the dark so they grow taller.
Put them in the fridge.
Move them to a light place.
questions.explanation: Plants need light to make food and stay green and strong. Seedlings in the dark stretch tall and thin, looking for light, but they are not healthy.

questions.stem: A cat in Dhaka has five kittens: two black, two striped and one white. What does this show?
options: The kittens are not from the same mother.
Young animals are like their parents but not exactly the same as each other.
The kittens' fur colour changed because of what they ate.
Only the black kittens are real cats.
questions.explanation: Young inherit features from their parents, but there is always variation. Kittens in one litter can have different colours and patterns.

questions.stem: The silk for a Rajshahi sari comes from the silkworm, which is the caterpillar (larva) of a moth.
questions.explanation: Silkworms eat mulberry leaves, then spin a cocoon of silk thread around themselves. Inside it becomes a pupa and later an adult moth.

questions.stem: A silk farmer's silkworms make 12 000 cocoons. One sari needs 3000 cocoons. How many saris can be made?
Tuli has a cough. Her cousin Rafi offers her some of the medicine his doctor gave him. What should Tuli do?
options: Take a small amount, just in case.
Take the same amount as Rafi.
Say no, and tell a trusted adult or a doctor about her cough.
Mix it with her juice.
questions.explanation: Medicine is a drug that changes how the body works. It is only safe if it is given to you by a doctor or trusted adult for you, in the right amount. Never share it.

questions.stem: In the simulation, with the wolves on, the fur colour that blends in with the ground becomes more common over many generations. Why?

sim.task: Open Natural Selection. Add a mate for the first bunny and choose an environment. Switch on the wolves, add a fur-colour mutation, and let the bunnies reproduce for many generations. Watch the population graph and the colours of the bunnies.

options: Bunnies with that fur survive longer and pass the colour on to their babies.
Bunnies change their fur colour when they see a wolf.
The wolves change the bunnies' fur colour.
Baby bunnies choose their own fur colour.
questions.explanation: Bunnies whose fur blends in are caught less often, so they have more babies. Babies inherit the fur colour from their parents, so that colour becomes more common.

questions.stem: In the simulation, a single bunny can change its own fur colour during its life to hide from the wolves.

sim.task: Open Natural Selection. Choose an environment, switch on the wolves and add a fur-colour mutation. Let the bunnies reproduce and watch whether any one bunny changes colour.

questions.explanation: A bunny keeps the fur colour it was born with. The population changes over generations because bunnies that blend in survive and pass their colour on.

questions.stem: Class 4C grew cress for 7 days (example data). Pot A had water, light and warmth: 6 cm. Pot B had no water: 0 cm. Pot C was in the dark: 7 cm, yellow and thin. Pot D was in a fridge: 1 cm. Pot C was the tallest. Does this mean cress grows best in the dark?
options: Yes, because the tallest seedlings are always the best.
No, because the Pot C seedlings were yellow and thin, so not healthy.
Yes, because plants do not need light.
No, because Pot C had no water.
questions.explanation: Height is not the only sign of growth. Seedlings without light grow tall and thin but stay yellow, and they cannot make food. Pot C did have water.

questions.stem: Mina wants to find out whether cress seeds need light to germinate. Which plan is the fairest test?
options: Put 10 seeds in a pot in the light and 20 seeds in a pot in the dark, and water both pots the same.
Put one pot in the light and water it every day, and put the other pot in the dark and never water it.
Use two pots with 10 seeds each, the same soil, water and warmth. Put one in the light and one in the dark. Count the seeds that germinate.
Put 10 seeds in each of two pots. Put one pot in the sun and the other in a dark fridge.
questions.explanation: In a fair test only the light changes. The other plans change more than one thing: the number of seeds, the water or the temperature.

questions.stem: Many frogs in Bangladesh are disappearing because ponds and wetlands are being filled in for building. Use the frog life cycle to explain why losing ponds is a problem for frogs.
questions.model_answer: Frogs lay their eggs in water, and tadpoles live in water and breathe with gills. Without ponds the eggs and tadpoles cannot survive, so no new frogs can grow up.
questions.explanation: The early stages of a frog's life cycle, the eggs and tadpoles, need water. If the ponds are filled in, the life cycle is broken and the frog population falls.

questions.stem: A silkworm grows about 10 000 times heavier during its month of eating mulberry leaves. Suppose (example) a newly hatched silkworm has a mass of 1 mg. Its mass after a month is about ___ g. (1 g = 1000 mg)
